title: Dates and timestamps as days and microseconds, as `sverify.sql.spark` writes them
description: `CAST(ts AS DATE)` of a TIMESTAMP_NTZ floors to its day (1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999 gives 1969-12-31), from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31.

`CAST(timestamp_micros(us) AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ)` and `unix_micros(CAST(ts AS TIMESTAMP_LTZ))`, under the session time zone UTC, are inverse: -1 is 1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999, and the range 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 round-trips.
`unix_date(a) - unix_date(b)` as BIGINTs is the difference of day numbers: −3652058, 3652058 and −1 for 0001-01-01/9999-12-31, the reverse, and 1969-12-31/1970-01-01.
reference: `UnFn.toDate` (days, rounding down), `UnFn.asTime` and `Time` microseconds since 1970, `BinFn.dateDiff` (the day numbers' difference).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark`'s `_writer_probes`, run locally with ANSI on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, which agree on each. pyspark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.13, macOS arm64, session time zone UTC (BASE_CONF); probes.json's header records the earlier homelab run.
